players.product: physics-plus-AI molecular discovery platform and Bunsen co-scientist

quarterly_data.signal: Total revenue for the second quarter of 2026 was $58.9 million. ACV excluding contribution was $22.6 million, a 23% increase over Q2 2025 and at the upper end of expectations, and first half 2026 ACV of $58.0 million represented 19% growth, with growth described as broad-based and driven by the top 20 pharma customers as well as biotech and materials science customers. Contribution ACV was $7 million, made up of $5 million from the Gates Foundation extending its funding for the Predictive Toxicology initiative and $2 million from Gates Ventures supporting battery research; contribution revenue fell to $3.4 million from $4.8 million in Q2 2025 as the initial Gates Foundation funding completed.
quarterly_data.figure: total revenue $58.9M; ACV ex-contribution $22.6M (+23%); H1 ACV $58.0M (+19%); contribution ACV $7M ($5M Gates Foundation + $2M Gates Ventures); contribution revenue $3.4M vs $4.8M

quarterly_data.signal: The planned shift to hosted licensing continued: hosted revenue reached 30% of the software total on a trailing four-quarter basis, up from 23% in Q2 2025 and 27% last quarter, and management reaffirmed the goal of 75% hosted by the end of 2028 after reaching 47% hosted this quarter. Software gross margin was 71% versus 76% in Q2 2025 because of the transition, and management repeated that every 1% increase in hosted revenue results in a $2 million-$3 million reduction in reported revenue depending on renewal quarter and contract length. A few customers were transitioned ahead of their renewal dates, which had an outsized impact on the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: TTM hosted 30% (vs 23% and 27%); 47% in the quarter; target 75% hosted by end-2028; software gross margin 71% vs 76%; each +1% hosted = $2M-$3M less revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Total operating expenses for Q2 were $74 million, a 6% decrease from $79 million in Q2 2025 and also down sequentially, driven by lower headcount, CRO and professional services fees. Total other income was $48.9 million, primarily a gain associated with the completion of Eli Lilly's acquisition of Ajax, and net income was $6 million versus a net loss of $43 million in Q2 2025. Fully diluted share count was 75.8 million.
quarterly_data.figure: opex $74M (-6% vs $79M); other income $48.9M; net income $6M vs -$43M; 75.8M diluted shares

quarterly_data.signal: Full year 2026 drug discovery revenue guidance was raised to $65 million-$75 million from a prior $55 million-$65 million because of the $10 million Ajax collaboration milestone, and full year operating expenses are expected to be lower than in 2025. For the third quarter of 2026 management guided ACV excluding contribution to $41 million-$45 million, compared with $38.3 million in Q3 2025 which included $2.2 million of contribution ACV, and reiterated that Q4 is the largest quarter and typically more than 50% of annual ACV.
quarterly_data.figure: drug discovery revenue guide raised to $65M-$75M (from $55M-$65M); Q3 2026 ACV ex-contribution $41M-$45M vs $38.3M; Q4 typically >50% of annual ACV

quarterly_data.signal: A new global collaboration with Simcere Pharmaceutical Group, announced in July, pairs Schrödinger's predict-first design approach with Simcere's pre-clinical and clinical execution, and Schrödinger is eligible for development and commercial milestone payments as well as tiered royalties on net sales.
quarterly_data.figure: Simcere global collaboration (announced July 2026): development and commercial milestones plus tiered royalties

quarterly_data.signal: Therapeutics value realized since 2020 spans co-founded companies Nimbus, Morphic and Structure and, most recently, Eli Lilly's $2.3 billion acquisition of Ajax. In June, data presented at the European Hematology Association for AJ11095, the phase I Type II JAK inhibitor that was the most advanced asset in the Ajax portfolio, provided initial clinical evidence that the selective molecule aligns with its differentiated target product profile, and management said multiple programs remain eligible for future milestones and royalties.
quarterly_data.figure: Lilly-Ajax $2.3B; AJ11095 phase I Type II JAK inhibitor EHA data (June 2026); co-founded Nimbus, Morphic, Structure

quarterly_data.signal: New products are a major contributor to growth: Predictive Toxicology, which predicts off-target binding risks before synthesis, has already contributed to 2026 ACV and is included in full year guidance, though management is not breaking out ACV by product and expects the product to keep contributing to growth for a number of years. RetroSynth is another new product contributing to growth and is part of the BMS agreement. Management also described an improved biotech end market, noting the number of IPOs this year is already about two times last year's level and that biotech customers are no longer struggling to raise funds at anywhere near last year's rate.
quarterly_data.figure: Predictive Tox contributing to 2026 ACV (not broken out); RetroSynth also contributing; biotech IPOs ~2x last year

quarterly_data.signal: Bunsen is being used inside Schrödinger's own therapeutics organization, where it supports target analysis and structural biology workflows as structure-based programs begin and the integrated analysis of DMPK, pharmacology and toxicology data in mature programs, accelerating the predict, design, make, test and analyze cycle. Longstanding collaborators NVIDIA and Google Cloud are providing additional tools and compute resources to support early access to Bunsen.
quarterly_data.figure: Bunsen deployed across internal therapeutics workflows; NVIDIA and Google Cloud supply tools and compute for early access

connects_to.relationship: enterprise deployment of Bunsen and molecular discovery software

contracts.signal: In Q&A management said BMS is one of Schrödinger's large customers and that, as a result of the agreement, BMS significantly scaled up its access to Schrödinger's technology. RetroSynth, one of the new products contributing to 2026 growth, is part of that agreement, and management framed the BMS implementation as a model for how large-scale deployment expands platform usage across the industry.
contracts.units: scaled-up enterprise access; RetroSynth included in the agreement
